name: Fertiliser supply
value: Gulf urea route disrupted, not shut
summary: Gulf fertiliser exports still face Hormuz attacks; escorted shipments recovering, so Alert unconfirmed
state: Hormuz carries about a third of world urea exports, and tankers were attacked in and near the strait again on 5–6 Nov (CBS News). CBS also reported that US escorts have brought Gulf shipments back near pre-war levels, and this run found no current report that the export route is closed or of urea prices up 60% in three months (farmdoc daily). The status moves to Watch; the Alert is unconfirmed.
for_you: Farmers face higher fertiliser costs and supply uncertainty, which can feed into food prices next season. Import-dependent countries in South Asia and Africa are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Watch: key export route disrupted; closure and >60% urea rise not confirmed this run

sources.title: farmdoc daily — Strait of Hormuz disruption scenarios and fertilizer purchasing risks

why: Fertiliser prices lead food prices by months; much of the world's urea and ammonia is exported from Russia, the Gulf and China.
drivers: Gas prices, Gulf shipping, export bans and quotas, sanctions, planting seasons.

rubric.alert: Urea up more than 60% in three months, several major exporters restricting at once, or a key export route closed.
rubric.watch: Urea up more than 30% in three months, or a major exporter restricts exports.
rubric.normal: Urea and ammonia prices within their normal range; no major export restrictions.
